headline: Delhi Police Defends Protest Denial Against Cockroach Janta Party
metaDescription: Delhi Police cited past misconduct and security concerns as reasons for denying the Cockroach Janta Party permission to protest at Jantar Mantar.
aiSummaryBullets: Delhi Police filed an affidavit in the Supreme Court justifying the refusal of a protest request for the Cockroach Janta Party.
Authorities cited historical incidents of violence and property damage associated with the party as primary reasons for the denial.
Leaders of the Cockroach Janta Party are scheduled to appear before the Sub-Divisional Executive Magistrate on December 11.
aiContextParagraph: The Delhi Police have formally justified their decision to prohibit a protest by the Cockroach Janta Party at Jantar Mantar through an affidavit submitted to the Supreme Court. Commissioner Anurag Kumar stated that the refusal was grounded in intelligence reports concerning potential public disorder and a history of non-compliance by party members during previous demonstrations. Police officials noted that prior gatherings linked to the organization resulted in physical violence and destruction of property, necessitating the current preventive restrictions. Concurrently, legal proceedings are ongoing regarding a trespassing case involving party leadership. Several members have been ordered to appear before the Sub-Divisional Executive Magistrate to address these concerns, with future hearings set for December. Meanwhile, party figure Ashutosh Ranka has announced the formation of new community clubs, signaling ongoing organizational activity despite the current legal scrutiny and challenges regarding public demonstration permits in the capital.
whyItIsViral: The story is tracked across two independent news outlets and maintains a moderate viral activity score due to active legal proceedings.
